card.name: Words just before a main clause starts
card.fires_on: Marks a point where a new clause or instruction is about to begin: the word "Follow" opening a sentence, or a comma ending an introductory phrase. It also fires partway through the name Decatur and the word decry.

modes.label: Sentence-opening "Follow"
modes.description: The verb Follow starts an instruction right after a sentence about limiting dosage and duration.
modes.example: Limit dosages and durations to the minimum required.<< Follow>> patients for signs and symptoms of respiratory depression

modes.label: Comma after an opening clause
modes.description: A comma closes an introductory or conditional phrase, just before the main instruction.
modes.example: If metformin-associated lactic acidosis is suspected<<,>> immediately discontinue sitagliptin and

modes.label: Start of "Dec-" words
modes.description: The pole fires on the "dec" piece of decry and of the name Decatur.
modes.example: Lt. Stephen<< Dec>>atur led the ship straight into Tripoli

card.writes: Weakly pushes toward words like "different" and "differently" and away from "provided" and "given"; the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It lights up at the hinge where a lead-in phrase ends and the main instruction begins, such as a sentence starting with "Follow".
